channel.title: DomCom Insure: Blog
channel.description: Timely guides on home and business insurance: rule changes, seasonal risks, claims tips and plain-English explainers for the UK, US and Europe.

item.title: Christmas gifts and your contents insurance
item.description: Expensive presents can push you over contents limits. Seasonal increases, single-item limits, gifts in the car, parcels and Christmas fire safety.

item.title: NFIP reauthorization: what the next deadline means for flood cover
item.description: The NFIP is authorized until 11 December 2026. What happens to new flood policies and renewals if it lapses, and how to protect your home.

item.title: Your winter home insurance checklist
item.description: Get your home and policy ready for winter: preventing burst pipes, storm prep, heating while you’re away, unoccupancy rules and what to do if water escapes.

item.title: Driving in Europe: insurance checks before you go
item.description: UK drivers don’t need a green card in the EU, but should still check foreign-use cover, breakdown, hire cars and documents. A pre-trip checklist.

item.title: How to make a home insurance claim
item.description: A practical guide to home insurance claims: the first hour, evidence to gather, loss adjusters, settlement offers and how to challenge one.

item.title: Storm damage and your home insurance
item.description: Storm season is here. What counts as a storm, what home insurance usually covers and excludes (like fences), and how to make a smooth claim.

item.title: Business interruption insurance explained
item.description: How business interruption insurance replaces lost profit after damage: gross profit, indemnity periods, extra costs and supplier extensions.

item.title: Cyber insurance basics for small businesses
item.description: What small businesses should know before buying cyber insurance: insurer questions, security basics, invoice fraud and breach reporting duties.

item.title: Hurricane deductibles explained
item.description: Many US coastal homeowners face a separate hurricane deductible, often 1% to 5% of the dwelling limit. How percentages and triggers work.

item.title: Non-disclosure and misrepresentation explained
item.description: Consumers must take reasonable care not to misrepresent; businesses must make a fair presentation. How UK law works and how to protect yourself.

item.title: Excesses and deductibles explained
item.description: How compulsory and voluntary excesses (and US deductibles) work, percentage deductibles, and how to choose an excess you can actually afford.

item.title: Unoccupied property insurance
item.description: Why home and landlord policies restrict cover after 30–60 days empty, what unoccupied property insurance covers, inspection conditions and probate properties.

item.title: Working from home and your insurance
item.description: Working from home as an employee or self-employed: what home insurance covers, when to tell your insurer and when you need business cover.

item.title: Public liability vs professional indemnity
item.description: Public liability covers injury and property damage; professional indemnity covers financial loss from your work. How to tell which you need.

item.title: Starting a business: your insurance checklist
item.description: The insurance to sort before you start trading: legal must-haves, what clients and landlords ask for, policies to update and covers to review later.

item.title: Monthly vs annual insurance payments
item.description: Paying car or home insurance monthly usually means borrowing. What the FCA’s 2026 premium finance study found and how to check the real cost.

item.title: Insurance Premium Tax (IPT) explained
item.description: UK Insurance Premium Tax explained: which policies pay the 12% standard rate, which pay 20%, what’s exempt (including life cover) and how it shows.

item.title: Under-insurance and the average clause
item.description: Insuring for too little can cut every claim, not just total losses. How the average clause works for home and business insurance, with a worked example.

item.title: Flood Re explained
item.description: How Flood Re helps UK homes in flood-risk areas get affordable insurance, which homes are eligible, why post-2009 homes are excluded and the 2039 end.

item.title: Employers’ liability insurance: the fines, and how to stay compliant
item.description: UK employers can be fined up to £2,500 a day for not holding employers’ liability insurance. Who must have it, the £5m minimum and the certificate rules.

item.title: The UK renewal pricing rules: what “no more price walking” means for you
item.description: Since 2022, UK home and car insurers can’t charge loyal customers more than new ones through the same channel. What the FCA rules mean for your renewal.
